newsitem.title: USA: Digital posts higher fourth-quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: Digital posts higher fourth-quarter earnings.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp. said Thursday it posted a profit in its fourth quarter, reversing a year-ago loss and continuing a string of gains set in motion by its 1996 restructuring.
Digital said growing sales of personal computers and units that connect networks of computers using Microsoft Corp.'s NT software were behind the improvement.

The profit of $123.9 million, or 75 cents per share, came on revenues of $3.5 billion. In the 1996 period, Digital lost $432.8 million, or $2.87 per share, on revenues of $3.7 billion. The 1996 result included a one-time restructuring charge of $492 million.
"I believe we're in the best position since the mid-1980s to take advantage of current and future opportunities," Digital Chief Executive Robert Palmer said.
The results were better than the 73 cents a share analysts surveyed by First Call had expected, and Digital's stock jumped $2.875 to $42.625 in consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading.
Analysts applauded the higher earnings, but said the lower revenues indicate Digital still must raise sales to sustain growth.
"It was OK, not great," said Steve Milunovich, an analyst at Morgan Stanley. "Revenues are a little light, margins were a little better."
Sales of computer systems based on Digital's Alpha microprocessors fell again year-over-year following sharp price cuts in January.

"It's just hard to get excited about this as a technology stock," said one analyst, who declined to be named. "The growth rate of Alpha is lackluster, the growth rate of PCs isn't really at the industry rate," he added.

But Chief Financial Officer Vincent Mullarkey said that the Maynard, Mass.-based company would show year-over-year growth in overall revenues as well as Alpha revenues as early as the current first quarter.
Digital said product revenues for the quarter were $2.0 billion, versus $2.1 billion a year ago while service revenues were $1.5 billion, compared with $1.6 billion a year earlier.
Digital also said it authorised the repurchase of up to 15 million shares of the 151.1 million outstanding shares of common stock.

Palmer said Digital's personal computer business achieved a higher level of profits for the third straight quarter, continuing a significant turnaround from the third quarter of fiscal 1996, when it was hurt by significant price competition and high levels of inventory.
Gross margins improved in the fiscal fourth quarter to 34.6 percent of revenues, up from 32.6 percent a year earlier, and were its best in more than three years.
"This reflects continuing improvements in product cost, productivity programmes and mix," Mullarkey said.
For the year, Digital earned $140.9 million, or 68 cents a share, on sales of $13 billion. A year earlier, it lost $111.8 million, or 97 cents a share, on sales of $14.6 billion.
